subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should unset existing installations automatically adopt the new blocking `local` readiness contract, or should stricter hosting-profile readiness require explicit operator selection?
rationale: This choice defines upgrade behavior for existing probes and the permanent public config, HTTP, and plugin API contract; implementation detail cannot safely substitute for maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve Existing Default
options.body: Keep current readiness semantics for unset installations and require explicit profile selection before additional predicates become blocking.

options.title: Adopt Local Automatically
options.body: Make `local` automatic and intentionally accept the changed blocking behavior with documented migration semantics and live upgrade proof.

options.title: Split The RFC
options.body: Advance the canonical result separately while deferring profile selection and plugin extensibility until their compatibility contracts are approved.

recommendation.title: Preserve Existing Default
recommendation.body: Keep current readiness semantics for unset installations and require explicit profile selection before additional predicates become blocking.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenClaw history connects this person most directly to container readiness and upgrade-compatibility decisions.
